note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — FINGERED HEAD
tiles.details: Kleberg bluestem is an introduced warm-season perennial. A complete head commonly bears 2–9 (broader sources 2–15) subdigitate racemes, often 3–7 cm long. Physically archived panel 9 shows source-identified flowering habit; remote panel 1 supplies another head view. Neither establishes exact glume hairs or species certainty. KR bluestem overlaps in raceme count; do not separate on head color or finger count alone.
tiles.short: Several narrow terminal fingers; count branches, then inspect real spikelet pairs.
tiles.status: VISIBLE HEAD; SPECIES CONFIRMATION NEEDS SPIKELET MACRO

tiles.heading: 02 · STEM NODE ≠ TRUE LIGULE
tiles.details: Panel 0 shows a genuine bearded STEM NODE. Panel 5 is now separately arrowed from a real CC BY 2.0 Harry Rose photograph: the green culm emerges from a lower enclosing sheath with visible pale hairy rim. This does NOT show the opened INNER blade/sheath ligule or prove its ~1–2 mm membrane. Do not confuse outer sheath-mouth hairs with the true ligule or with the unrelated long node beard. Prioritize a species-labelled opened inner leaf junction at a real 1-mm scale from a Texas specimen.
tiles.short: Compare the real node beard against the separate photographed sheath; ligule still unseen
tiles.status: TWO GROSS ARROWS ON REAL SHEATH PHOTO; TRUE INNER LIGULE REMAINS MISSING

tiles.heading: 03 · ROOTED BASE AND BASAL RACEME PAIRS
tiles.details: Kleberg may be tufted, ascending or stoloniferous with low stems rooting at nodes. At the base of some flowering racemes, 0–6 spikelet pairs are male or sterile rather than normal fertile pairs. KR can spread under mowing; habit alone is not decisive. Photograph a connected rooted Texas plant and the bottom of one intact raceme.
tiles.short: Check the rooted perennial crown, creeping lower shoots and sterile basal pairs.

tiles.heading: 04 · PAIRED MATURE SPIKELETS
tiles.details: At a rachis joint find the sessile fertile spikelet and pedicelled male/sterile companion. FNA describes sessile units about 2.5–5 mm; ranges vary by treatment. Archived panel 6 shows attached paired spikelets, while panel 3 shows a photographer-labelled close-up of the two units and glume hairs. Neither supplies a Texas same-specimen calibrated 1-mm view of basal raceme pairs, exact insertion and individual glume length.
tiles.short: Sessile fertile 2.5–5 mm beside a usually awnless pedicelled companion.
tiles.status: REAL PAIR PHOTO; ATTACHED MEASURED PAIR NEEDED

tiles.heading: 05 · GLUMES, REDUCED LEMMA AND AWN
tiles.details: The sessile lower glume is often broad/obtuse, typically 5–9-veined in Flora of China and hairy along its upper margins. The upper glume is keeled; the lower sterile floret has a thin lemma, while the reduced fertile upper lemma produces one bent/twisted awn, often about 13–22 mm in FNA (other floras 8–25 mm). The awn is NOT a glume spine. Source photos show gross awn and dissection, not a measured Texas glume/lemma.
tiles.short: Blunt lower glume with upper-edge hairs; ONE bent fertile-lemma awn.

tiles.heading: 06 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: Use archived Kleberg flowering panel 9 and paired-spikelet panel 3 alongside clearly OTHER-species KR panel 7 and silky node panel 8. KR may have stiff papilla-based hairs on the upper blade near its collar; silky and native cane bluestems can also have white-bearded culm nodes. Compare actual rooted bases, true inner ligules, attached racemes, mature sessile/pedicelled pairs, lower-glume margins and awn origins. If uncertain, record bluestem candidate and preserve native plants.
tiles.short: Separate Kleberg from KR, silky and native bluestems using several structures.

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: KLEBERG BLUESTEM (introduced): LOOK HERE FIRST at the complete cluster of slender terminal racemes, then trace an attached fertile sessile spikelet and its pedicelled companion. Check the true culm node and basal shoots, but a conspicuous white node beard is variable in North American material and also occurs in silky and native cane bluestems; do NOT require it. Verify the broad/obtuse lower glume, upper marginal hairs and twisted fertile-lemma awn under magnification. KR bluestem overlaps in raceme count and color, so never decide from a purple head or hair ring alone.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: STEM NODE: white spreading hairs at the true joint on the blue-background picture. Do NOT mistake a leaf-blade collar for the joint.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Panel 0 shows a genuine bearded STEM NODE. Panel 5 is now separately arrowed from a real CC BY 2.0 Harry Rose photograph: the green culm emerges from a lower enclosing sheath with visible pale hairy rim. This does NOT show the opened INNER blade/sheath ligule or prove its ~1–2 mm membrane. Do not confuse outer sheath-mouth hairs with the true ligule or with the unrelated long node beard. Prioritize a species-labelled opened inner leaf junction at a real 1-mm scale from a Texas specimen.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Kleberg may be tufted, ascending or stoloniferous with low stems rooting at nodes. At the base of some flowering racemes, 0–6 spikelet pairs are male or sterile rather than normal fertile pairs. KR can spread under mowing; habit alone is not decisive. Photograph a connected rooted Texas plant and the bottom of one intact raceme.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: KR vs Kleberg: both introduced grasses have clustered relatively long fingerlike racemes. Kleberg commonly has spreading LONG WHITE HAIR ring at true nodes and sometimes creeping rooted basal shoots; KR may have short/appressed nodal hairs plus distinctive stiff papilla-based hairs on UPPER blade just above collar. Kleberg lower glume often broadly obtuse with long upper marginal hairs; KR glume often more tapering, pedicellate spikelet generally hairless in local treatment. Compare mature attached spikelet pairs, glumes, pedicels and basal sterile pairs with 1-mm scale. D. sericeum ALSO has heavily hairy nodes; its typically sessile/subsessile densely silky racemes and specific glume marginal fringe require matched macro.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: Kleberg node
panels.caption: This Australian specimen has an obvious LONG WHITE HAIR RING at its true stem NODE, not the blade/sheath collar. IMPORTANT: North American Flora of North America treatment also describes D. annulatum nodes as GLABROUS or SHORT-PUBESCENT, so a white beard is NOT a mandatory Texas ID character. Silky bluestem may be similarly bearded; inspect paired reproductive spikelets, glumes, ligule and growth form.
panels.creator: Harry Rose (Macleay Grass Man)
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: TWO SPIKELETS — pedicelled companion, awned partner and glume hairs
panels.caption: The paired reproductive units were photographed separated against a gray background. The left unit has a conspicuous slender pedicel below; the right unit carries a tall awn. Long glume-margin hairs are visible. Photographer describes spikelets to approximately 4 mm, but the image itself has no metric scale. No original branch attachment is visible, so don't infer their exact position on an intact rachis.
panels.creator: Harry Rose (Macleay Grass Man)
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: DISSECTED FERTILE SPIKELET — actual upper and lower glumes, lemma awn
panels.caption: REAL DISSECTION, NOT a distant head: author Harry Rose identifies the left bract as UPPER GLUME, the long awn rising from the fertile lemma, ovary and translucent sterile lemma in the center, and the HAIRY LOWER GLUME at right. Genuine visible structures; no calibrated millimeter ruler, so don't infer exact measurements or a Hays voucher.
panels.creator: Harry Rose (Macleay Grass Man)
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: Kleberg bluestem — inspected source photograph
panels.caption: Original photo visibly shows an erect bundle of slender pigmented seed-bearing branches and long fine awns. It cannot resolve the diagnostic WHITE RING at the vegetative stem node, which lies off-frame.
panels.creator: Macleay Grass Man (Harry Rose)

memory_rule: KLEBERG often has LONG SPREADING node beard + many fingers; KR often has PAPILLA hairs above leaf collar and sometimes short node hairs. Both have terminal fingers, and silky also has a node beard. Need attached mature glumes.
safety_note:
These are licensed public photo references from Australian source plants, not independent Hays vouchers or same-plant photographs. Full local plant, paired mature spikelets and blade collar are still needed.
2026-10-27: panel 5 actually archived and pixels reviewed. Two new arrows on GREEN CULM and surrounding SHEATH, not inner ligule. Inner true membrane and rooted base remain missing; 6-role score 4/6 (66.7%), rights/deployment checks separate.
field_rule: When both are introduced, the management group may be the same, but botany cards must not overclaim a species. Also rule out native cane/little/big/silver bluestems before removal.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
